newsitem.title: CHILE: Codelco details terms of 1997 cathode contracts.
newsitem.headline: Codelco details terms of 1997 cathode contracts.

text.p: Chile's state copper company Codelco said it will charge a $30/tonne premium next year over base price for grade A copper cathodes delivered to six European ports with varying premiums to other destinations.
The $30 premium will apply to cathodes delivered CIF to Rotterdam, Dunkirk, Bilbao, Liverpool, Salerno and Livorno, said Juan Eduardo Herrera, Codelco's senior sales vice president, in a statement.
"Premiums for deliveries to other destinations will reflect respective costs of delivery and market conditions," he said.
The base price for the cathode sales will be the London Metals Exchange Grade "A" copper cash settlement quotation.
All other contract conditions are unchanged from previous years, said Herrera.
Codelco is the world's largest copper producer with output of around 1.2 million tonnes last year.
